input: tiles is an uppercase-English string of length n in [1,7]. Collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse/accessor-backed collections. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. Every collection length and computed allocation size fits [0,4294967295], with padded sizes explicitly included. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is allowed. Preconditions are not runtime-checked, and allocation/resource capacity or completion is not guaranteed by declared bounds. Python integer inputs are plain int, excluding bool.
return: Integer number of distinct nonempty letter sequences constructible using at most the available multiplicity of each letter.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs and caller-held aliases remain unchanged; working state is private. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Each recursion node contributes one distinct next-letter prefix. At n = 7 with all letters distinct, the total is 7 + 42 + 210 + 840 + 2520 + 5040 + 5040 = 13699, bounding every recursive count and partial sum. All integer inputs/intermediates remain within [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: With S distinct nonempty constructible sequences: O(n+26*(S+1)) time and O(26+n) auxiliary storage including the histogram and bounded recursive stack. No output sequences are materialized. Bounds include ordinary built-in operations/allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop and any explicitly stated hash/sort behavior.

helpers.name: count_sequences
helpers.contract: Counts all nonempty sequences from a private 26-entry nonnegative letter histogram with total count at most 7. Choosing a letter consumes one copy, recursion counts continuations, and undo restores the histogram exactly on normal return. Equal copies are never treated as distinct choices.
helpers.cost: For S distinct nonempty sequences from the supplied histogram, O(26*(S+1)) time and O(n+1) recursive stack depth for n remaining tiles; all counters and recursive calls are included. Its complete definition is 251 UTF-8 bytes; separator newlines count toward total source bytes.
